name: The seven feature axes a reader chooses an engine on were recorded for a minority of engines - a dated audit of which are stated, which are absent, and which are affirmatively NO
symptom: A reader comparing engines on 'does it do speculative decoding, chunked prefill, prefix caching, disaggregated prefill/decode, structured output, multi-model, multimodal' finds these recorded for some engines and simply missing for others, with no way to tell 'lacks it' from 'nobody checked'. Audited on 2026-10-04 across all 103 engine records by scanning each record's serialized text for axis-specific vocabulary, then reading primary docs for the engines that mattered. RESULT: of the 103 engine records, 29 recorded none of the seven axes at all, and a further 15 recorded exactly one. Only 6 engines recorded three or more.
root_cause: The axes were recorded opportunistically - when an engine's author happened to mention speculative decoding in a README, that got written into notable_features, and nobody went looking for the axes that were not mentioned. The failure mode is silent and it is the dangerous kind: an absent field in a comparison table reads as 'no' to a hurried reader, which is wrong for an engine that supports the feature and simply was never checked. This audit exists so that an absent field reads as 'unstated' instead.
workaround: For the seven axes, treat the only three legitimate values as YES (with a source), NO (affirmatively documented as absent, with a source), and UNSTATED (nobody checked - the default for a gap). Never infer NO from silence. Where this audit found a genuine YES it is named below with its source; where it found an affirmative NO it is named as such; everything else is UNSTATED and should stay that way until someone reads the engine's own docs. Concretely, the gaps worth closing next, in the order a reader is most likely to hit them: engines serving production traffic whose axis status is entirely UNSTATED ([[triton-inference-server]], [[niche-ray-serve]], [[niche-kserve]], [[nvidia-dynamo]], [[llm-d]] - all four axes are unstated for all of these), the consumer-local engines ([[ollama]], [[jan]], [[koboldcpp]], [[llamafile]], [[mlc-llm]]), and the ASR/image engines where 'speculative decoding' does not even apply but 'chunked prefill' and 'prefix caching' might ([[faster-whisper]], [[whisper-cpp]], [[openai-whisper]], [[apple-coreml]]).
notes: WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, stated per axis as of 2026-10-04. SPECULATIVE DECODING - confirmed YES from vendor docs on 2026-10-04 for [[vllm]] (thirteen published methods: EAGLE, LiLiCorr, MTP, Draft Model, PARD, MLP speculator, N-gram, Suffix decoding, Hidden State Extraction, Custom Proposer Backend, Dynamic Speculative Decoding, Adaptive Verification, Per-Request Acceptance Metrics), [[sglang]] (EAGLE-2/EAGLE-3, MTP, UNO, DFLASH, classic draft model, NGRAM), [[llama-cpp]] (eleven algorithms across three families: draft-simple, draft-eagle3, draft-mtp, draft-dflash, draft-dspark, ngram-simple, ngram-map-k, ngram-map-k4v, ngram-mod, ngram-cache), [[exllamav3]] (vendor README states it), [[openvino-genai]] (already recorded). UNSTATED for the rest. Two records that exist in this repo cover the technique as a system rather than as an engine feature and are not engine-axis answers: [[niche-eagle]] and [[niche-medusa]]. CHUNKED PREFILL - confirmed YES only for [[vllm]], [[sglang]] and [[vllm-gaudi]] (already recorded); UNSTATED for every other engine including [[tensorrt-llm]] and [[text-generation-inference]], which is worth noting because chunked prefill is a scheduling behaviour a reader would assume any modern engine has. PREFIX CACHING - the widest-covered axis and the one where the mechanisms genuinely differ, which is why a boolean would lose information: [[sglang]] radix tree over the KV cache (RadixAttention, any shared prefix not just an exact match); [[ktransformers]] three-tier GPU-CPU-DISK prefix cache reuse, the only engine here with a disk tier, and unsurprising once you know its weights do not fit in VRAM; [[openvino-genai]] caches 'fragments of previous generation requests'; [[llama-cpp]] has no named feature but the mechanisms underneath - a shared unified KV buffer, slot-prompt-similarity matching at default 0.10, idle-slot prompt-cache persistence, and up to 32 per-slot context checkpoints. DISAGGREGATED PREFILL/DECODE - YES on [[tensorrt-llm]] and [[vllm]] already; [[niche-lmdeploy-turbomind]] gains a qualified YES ('[2025/06] DeepSeek PD Disaggregation deployment is now supported through integration with DLSlime and Mooncake' - i.e. via two OTHER projects' integration, not an in-tree scheduler, the same distinction applied to vLLM's third-party connectors). vLLM's docs also contribute the caveat worth carrying forward: 'Disaggregated prefill DOES NOT improve throughput'. STRUCTURED OUTPUT - [[vllm]] (xgrammar and guidance backends, on by default in the OpenAI-compatible server, with an API break: guided_json/guided_regex/guided_choice/guided_grammar/guided_whitespace_pattern/structural_tag/guided_decoding_backend all REMOVED in v0.12.0) and [[onnxruntime-genai]] (grammar specification for tool calling is an in-engine first-class capability, unusual at that EPU breadth). UNSTATED elsewhere, including [[tensorrt-llm]]. MULTI-MODEL - the axis most often confused with multi-SURFACE: [[vllm]] and [[text-generation-inference]] (Rust router) already recorded; [[niche-lmdeploy-turbomind]] confirmed via a proxy/distribution server doc. [[mlc-llm]]'s existing 'One MLCEngine behind Python, REST, JavaScript/WebGPU, iOS and Android' is about serving SURFACES, not about serving several models at once, and the audit flags that as a distinction to preserve rather than an axis answer. MULTIMODAL - confirmed YES for [[exllamav3]], [[openvino-genai]] (image AND video, LLaVa/MiniCPM-V), [[ktransformers]] (GLM-5.3-flash, 2026-08-26), [[onnxruntime-genai]] (stated per-architecture, which is the more honest form: LFM2 language+vision+speech, Phi language+vision, Qwen language+vision). [[llama-cpp]] gains the most detailed answer in the repo from tools/server/README.md: --mmproj, --mmproj-url, --mmproj-auto, --mmproj-offload, --mmproj-device, --image-min-tokens/--image-max-tokens for dynamic-resolution models. NEGATIVE FINDINGS THAT ARE REAL NEGATIVES, not gaps: llama.cpp's server surface has NO disaggregated prefill/decode mode and no chunked-prefill knob, and no multimodal/audio projector path beyond the mmproj vision flags above. AFFIRMATIVE NO for vLLM multimodal on AMD: the existing [[vllm]] record already records that the enc-dec feature is unsupported on ROCm, which is a per-platform NO and a different claim from a general one. UNVERIFIED BY ME: [[mlc-llm]] is a stated-as-UNSTATED rather than a stated-as-NO - a keyword scan of its README returned zero hits on all seven axes, but the README is a short project overview and the authoritative per-model surface (the MLC model library) was NOT enumerated, so absence of evidence there is not evidence of absence; [[sglang]] chunked prefill and [[tensorrt-llm]] structured output were confirmed only from docs read on 2026-10-04 and should be re-checked against a specific release before being quoted as release-specific facts; and no axis was checked for [[fastertransformer]] beyond what its existing record already says.
